thread:
alex: Heads up — ACME prod is getting 500s on our tool-invoke endpoint since last night. Customer reports ~10% failure rate and increased retry billing.

alex: Example error from logs: 
```
Error: validation_failed: field 'recipient_ids' expected array, got string
runtime: validator.js:45 throw new ValidationError(...)
HTTP 500 -> 422 in runtime, then endpoint surfaced as 500 to caller
```

julie: can you paste the exact request you sent (body + headers) and the runtime/version?

alex: curl we used in prod test: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/tool/invoke \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"tool": "send_notifications", "args": {"recipient_ids": "12345", "message": "hi"}}'
```
(note: recipient_ids is a string here — customer SDK serializes single id as string)

omar: that payload used to be accepted because we had a permissive coercion layer. I pushed the strict param validation change in runtime v4.2.0 last week that enforces declared JSON schema types. If the declared schema is an array, strings will now trigger validation errors.

ming: logs show runtime validated against schema: 
```
{"path":"/tool/invoke","schema":{"args":{"recipient_ids":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}}}}}
validation error: /args/recipient_ids: expected array
```

alex: customer says their client used to send single-ID strings and relied on server to wrap into an array. After the runtime rollout they started getting 500s and retried — billing spiked.

julie: OK — we need a repro matrix and short-term mitigation. Omar, can runtime add a compatibility shim that coerces single string -> [string] when schema says array? We should also consider a telemetry flag to identify how many callers send string vs array.

omar: quick mitigation: yes, can add an opt-in compatibility mode. Patch idea (pseudo): 
```
if (schema.type === 'array' && typeof value === 'string') {
  value = [value]; // adapt legacy clients
}
```
I'll open a hotfix branch and a canary release for the shim.

ming: repro steps I ran locally: 
1) start runtime v4.2.0 with strict validation on
2) POST payload with recipient_ids as string (curl above)
3) observe 422 validation -> gateway returns 500 to client
4) change payload to recipient_ids: ["12345"] -> success

julie: alex — please collect a minimal failing request/response pair from the customer (include X-Request-ID and timestamps). We'll need billing team to evaluate token/retry cost. Add customer impact: 10% calls failed, some clients retried rapidly causing spikes.

alex: sending packet capture and X-Request-IDs to you now. Also note one customer reported the key name is actually "recipientIdList" in their older SDK — looks like a naming drift across client versions. So two problems: type (string vs array) and key name mismatch.

omar: good catch — I'll add both fixes: (1) shim to coerce string->array, (2) fallback to look up alias keys at parse time (recipientIdList -> recipient_ids). Patch snippet: 
```
args.recipient_ids = args.recipient_ids || args.recipientIdList;
if (typeof args.recipient_ids === 'string') args.recipient_ids = [args.recipient_ids];
```
Will add feature flag so enterprises can enable strict mode.

deploy-bot: Hotfix branch "runtime/compat-recipient-array" created by omar. CI triggered.

julie: Priority: P1 customer impact. Escalating to eng-runtime for hotfix deploy and to billing for cost reconciliation. alex — please open a support ticket with customer-facing mitigation steps: 1) temporary client-side fix (wrap IDs in array), 2) timeline for hotfix.

alex: Will open ticket and paste mitigation. Also adding recommended patch for server-side fallback in the ticket so acme can evaluate short-term proxy if needed.

ming: after hotfix can we add telemetry to count occurrences of string vs array and alias key usage? That will help avoid future regressions.

omar: yes — adding metrics + rollout plan to PR. Will post deployment ETA in this thread.

julie: thanks everyone. Please keep updates concise in thread. We'll follow up with billing + SRE postmortem if needed.
